prompt: Company profile: Metal stamping plant in Kenosha, Wisconsin; 150 employees. Situation: A new high-tonnage press line was commissioned. Area noise monitoring in the press bay shows employee full-shift exposures around 88 dBA TWA; the rest of the plant is below 80 dBA. About 25 employees work in the press bay. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
Based on the scenario provided, here are the compliance obligations to be entered into the register.

**Note on Regulatory Jurisdiction:**
Since the plant is located in Kenosha, Wisconsin, it is subject to the **Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)** regulations, which operates an OSHA-approved State Plan. Wisconsin has adopted federal OSHA standards by reference (specifically SPS 332 for General Industry). Therefore, the requirements below cite the relevant Wisconsin Administrative Code chapters alongside their federal OSHA counterparts.

### 1. Obligation: Hearing Conservation Program Implementation
*   **Requirement:** The employer must administer a continuing, effective hearing conservation program whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) of 85 dBA (Action Level).
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(c); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** The monitoring data shows exposures of 88 dBA TWA for press bay employees. Since 88 dBA is greater than the 85 dBA Action Level, the obligation is triggered for the ~25 employees in the press bay.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Internal audit of the Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) elements (audiometric testing, training, hearing protection).
    *   *Timing:* Continuous program administration required; internal audit annually.

### 2. Obligation: Engineering and Administrative Controls
*   **Requirement:** When employees are exposed to noise levels above 90 dBA TWA (Permissible Exposure Limit), feasible engineering or administrative controls shall be implemented. If such controls fail to reduce sound levels below 90 dBA, personal protective equipment (PPE) must be used.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(b); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** Current exposures are 88 dBA TWA. While this is below the 90 dBA PEL, it exceeds the Action Level. Best practice and OSHA interpretation dictate that the employer must still consider engineering controls to reduce exposure, though strict mandatory implementation of engineering controls is not triggered until exposures reach 90 dBA. However, the company must document that it has evaluated the feasibility of engineering controls (e.g., enclosing the new press line) to satisfy the "effective" HCP requirement.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Feasibility study or noise control engineering assessment.
    *   *Timing:* One-time evaluation following the commissioning of the new press line; re-evaluation if processes change.

### 3. Obligation: Audiometric Testing Program
*   **Requirement:** The employer shall establish and maintain an audiometric testing program for all employees exposed at or above the Action Level (85 dBA).
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(g); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** Mandatory for the 25 employees in the press bay.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Review of audiometric testing records and professional reviewer qualifications.
    *   *Timing:* Baseline audiograms within 6 months of first exposure (or 12 months if mobile test van used with interim protection); annual audiograms thereafter.

### 4. Obligation: Hearing Protection Provision
*   **Requirement:** Employers must make hearing protectors available to all employees exposed at or above the Action Level (85 dBA) at no cost. Use is mandatory for employees who have not yet had a baseline audiogram, who have experienced a Standard Threshold Shift (STS), or whose exposure exceeds 90 dBA.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(i); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** The company must provide hearing protection to the 25 press bay employees. Since the exposure (88 dBA) is below 90 dBA, use is mandatory only for those with an STS or pending baseline, though mandatory use policies are common best practice.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Inspection of PPE availability and usage; review of STS records.
    *   *Timing:* Ongoing (monthly/quarterly inspections).

### 5. Obligation: Employee Training
*   **Requirement:** The employer shall train each employee exposed at or above the Action Level in the hazards of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(k); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** Mandatory for the 25 press bay employees.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Review of training records and content; employee interviews.
    *   *Timing:* Upon initial assignment; annually thereafter.

### 6. Obligation: Noise Exposure Recordkeeping
*   **Requirement:** The employer shall maintain accurate records of employee exposure measurements for at least 2 years and audiometric test records for the duration of the affected employee’s employment.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(m); Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.095.
*   **Applicability:** The company must retain the monitoring data showing 88 dBA TWA and all audiometric results for the 25 affected employees.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Records retention audit.
    *   *Timing:* Annually.

### 7. Obligation: Wisconsin DSPS Annual Summary (OSHA 300 Log)
*   **Requirement:** Employers must record work-related hearing loss cases (Standard Threshold Shift) on the OSHA 300 Log and post the annual summary (OSHA 300A) from February 1 to April 30.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1904; Wisconsin Admin. Code SPS 332.
*   **Applicability:** If any of the 25 employees suffer an STS (a change in hearing threshold of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz), it must be recorded. The new press line increases the risk of STS.
*   **ISO Clause Mapping:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Compliance Obligations).
*   **Evaluation Method & Timing:**
    *   *Method:* Review of OSHA 300 Log for accuracy; verification of posting.
    *   *Timing:* Annually (Log maintained throughout year; posted Feb 1–April 30).
